8月5日晚10时许，25岁的宁波籍男子沈永章（Sung Yung-chong），住同山路1049号，在圆明园路安美洋行（Anderson, Meyer & Co.）担任铜匠，在从朋友家返回途中，经过达罗克路（Darroch Road）附近的北四川路延伸段时，遭遇两名敌军士兵，被其任意逮捕并带至陆战队总部，关押在一间黑屋内。他未受审问，也未得到任何食物或饮水。昨天上午，两名敌军士兵走近他，强迫他喝下两杯白色液体。沈永章虽从气味中知悉杯中物为硝酸，但意识到已无逃生机会，只得违心接受，然而因气味刺鼻，他无法吞咽并发生呕吐，结果全身被硝酸灼伤。两名敌军士兵拍手大笑。不久后他们 leaving him alone（留他独自一人）。沈永章趁此机会立即冲出，但很快被敌军士兵发现并立即展开追捕。沈永章走投无路，跳入附近的一条小河沟中，因会游泳，他在水中藏匿了近两个小时。后来，见追捕者已离开，他便从水中出来，逃回家中。
家人见其模样大为惊恐，在得知其经历后，向榆林路警察局报案。因此，警方于昨日下午将沈永章送往医院治疗。他目前正在接受医疗救治，能否存活尚待观察。

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

MEMBER OF PEACE PRESERVATION CORPS ARRESTED BY
JAPANESE MARINES

At 9 a.m. yesterday, a Chinese wearing khaki uniform, having the appearance of a member of the Peace Preservation Corps, arrived at the corner of Gordon Road and Penang Road in a ricsha. It happened that nearby was the residence of the manager of "Naigai," where a party of Japanese marines are stationed. Seeing the approach of the member of the Peace Preservation Corps, the Japanese marine posted there at once raised his rifle and ordered him to stop. He was arrested and taken to the marine post.

Upon receipt of the above report, detectives and policemen of Gordon Road Station went to the place to investigate. A party of Chinese and foreign detectives led by a foreign Inspector called at the marine post in question and succeeded in bringing the arrested member of the Peace Preservation Corps to the Police Station.

At the Police Station the man made the following statement:- "My name is Chang Tsing (張俊), age 23, a member of the Peace Preservation Corps, Third Squadron, Lih Sz Hsien (溧水縣), Kiangsu Province. A few days ago, my wife ran away with her sweetheart. Upon receiving a report that my wife was in Shanghai working in a certain factory, I came here in order to find her, having obtained permission from my senior officer. I reside in room No.1 in the Yuan Sung Hotel (元生旅館), Ningpo Road. As I had learned that my wife is working in a factory in the Western District, I took a ricsha at 10 a.m. to-day to convey me to that place. I was arrested on arrival."

At 3 p.m. the Police handed the man over to the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau for disposal.

维持会成员被日本海军陆战队逮捕

昨日上午9时，一名身穿卡其色制服、看似维持会成员的中国人乘坐人力车到达戈登路与槟榔路转角处。恰巧附近是“内海”（Naigai，音译）经理的住所，有一队日本海军陆战队士兵驻守于此。日本海军陆战队哨兵见该维持会成员走近，立即举枪命令其停下。该人被捕并被带至海军陆战队哨所。

接到上述报告后，戈登路警署的侦探和警察前往该处调查。由一名外籍巡官带领的一队中西侦探前往该海军陆战队哨所，成功将被捕的维持会成员带至警察局。

在警察局，该人作出如下陈述：“我叫张俊（Chang Tsing），23岁，系江苏省溧水县（Lih Sz Hsien）维持会第三中队成员。数日前，我妻子与情人私奔。收到报告说我妻子在上海某工厂做工，我在获得上级军官许可后，来此寻找她。我住在宁波路元生旅馆（Yuan Sung Hotel）1号房间。因得知我妻子在西区一家工厂工作，我今天上午10时乘人力车前往该处。到达后即被捕。”

下午3时，警方将该人移交给上海市政府警察局处理。

My name is Tsu Liang, aged 22 years, native of

to South and did not act wrongly in any way. Regarding

realise that I did so. However, the Japanese sentry
ordered me to stop and wait for a while in the Branch
Office. Later a Japanese policeman took me to the station
where I was questioned by a Japanese and Chinese detective
in respect of this case.

The above statement is true.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, April 28, 1937.

Shanghai Incident Averted
WITH APPREHENSION we view the action
of a small Irakian schoolboy who thumb-
ed his nose at a sentry before the Japanese
Landing Party headquarters in Shanghai Mon-
day afternoon and the subsequent grave
developments.
Justly incensed, the sentry caused the
offender (from the Public and Thomas Han-
bury School) to be taken into custody by a
Japanese member of the Shanghai Municipal
Police and a detailed report was made.
Vice-Admiral K. Okawachi, commander of
the Landing Party, in due course made formal
demand for an apology; with the result that
parents of the boy appeared at headquarters,
complied with this demand, and the boy was
released—a chastened and wiser lad, let us
trust.
The potentialities of the situation thus
happily liquidated are obvious. Such reckless
international impudence might well provoke the
most horrifying of consequences. Nose-thumb-
ing has much distinguished precedent, of
course, including the action of a prominent
European official toward the press gallery at
Geneva. But Shanghai is not Geneva and we
do not wish it to become Spain.
Let there be no international nose-thumb-
ing in future, or at least toward the Japanese
Naval Landing Party. If Irakian or other
schoolboys feel that they simply must thumb
their noses, let them come down and do it at
this office. We will reciprocate in a spirit
of good clean fun and use both hands.

上海事件得以避免

我们怀着忧虑的心情看待一名伊拉克小学生在周一下午于上海日本海军陆战队总部前对哨兵竖拇指做蔑视手势（thumbed his nose），以及随后引发的严重事态发展。

哨兵正当愤怒，致使该肇事者（来自公立学校及托马斯·汉伯里学校）被一名上海公共租界工部局警务处的日籍警员拘捕，并提交了详细报告。

日本海军陆战队指挥官大川内（K. Okawachi）少将在适当时候正式要求道歉；结果是，男孩的父母前往总部，满足了这一要求，男孩获释——希望这是一个受到惩戒且变得更明智的少年。

如此幸得化解的局势所蕴含的潜在危险是显而易见的。这种鲁莽的国际无礼行为很可能引发最可怕的后果。当然，竖拇指蔑视手势有着许多著名的先例，包括一位欧洲高官在日内瓦对新闻席所做的举动。但上海不是日内瓦，我们不希望它变成西班牙。

今后不要再有国际性的竖拇指蔑视行为，或者至少不要针对日本海军陆战队。如果伊拉克或其他国家的学童觉得他们非要做这个手势不可，让他们下来对本报社做这个手势吧。我们将以良好、纯粹的娱乐精神予以回敬，并且双手并用。

Shanghai Mercantile Press (上海商報) published the following
article on January 29, written by one Kiang Sz (江思) :-

STREET INCIDENTS

One frequently meets with a search party on
North Sz.chuen Road whether during the day or night.
Whenever I turn to Kiangwan Road from the Hongkew Park,
I have always been searched by the marines of our friendly
nation.

One night, as I was walking alone, a voice
said, "Stop!" A blue-uniformed marine wearing a steel
helmet with a long gun on his shoulder approached and
searched me; he even put his hand in my pockets. After
the search, he said "Go!" I returned home in great
wrath.

A friend of mine tells me that on one occasion
his outside clothing was destroyed by a Japanese marine
because he had looked at a party of marines.
Hearing of this, another friend said: "You
were fortunate. If you had resisted, you would have been
slapped, or the marine might have fired at you".

Two days later, I received information that
a certain friend of mine had been stabbed and seriously
wounded for refusing to submit to a search.

The fragrant smell of powder from a Japanese
brothel next door caused several youths to peep at the
brothel. They were noticed by a military officer who
went to the house with drawn pistol.
"We have not done anything to offend you",
said the female house tenant. The sounds of slapping of
the face were heard. That night, the house was surrounded
by two groups of Japanese marines who searched the place
and intimidated the inmates.

There is a Chinese school on North Sz.chuen
Road. Opposite to it is a Japanese home.
Suddenly, a telephone message was received
accusing the students of peeping at a Japanese woman
taking her bath.
Investigations showed that while the students
were having some fun among themselves, the Japanese woman
opposite was taking her bath.
That evening, three groups of Japanese
marines arrived at the school on motor cycles and searched
the school.
Next morning, two of the students came to
the school saying that a Japanese ronin had snatched away
a satchel.

《上海商报》于1月29日刊登了由江思（Kiang Sz）撰写的以下文章：-

街头事件

无论白天还是夜晚，在北四川路上经常遇到搜查队。每当我从虹口公园转向江湾路时，总会受到我们要好邻邦的海军陆战队员的搜查。

一天晚上，当我独自走路时，一个声音说：“站住！”一名身穿蓝色制服、头戴钢盔、肩扛长枪的海军陆战队员走近并搜查了我；他甚至把手伸进我的口袋。搜查结束后，他说：“走！”我满怀怒火回到家中。

一位朋友告诉我，有一次，他的外衣被一名日本海军陆战队员撕毁，原因只是他看了一眼一队海军陆战队员。
听到此事，另一位朋友说：“你很幸运。如果你反抗，你会挨耳光，或者海军陆战队员可能会向你开枪”。

两天后，我收到消息，我的一位朋友因拒绝接受搜查而被刺成重伤。

隔壁一家日本妓院飘出的脂粉香气引得几名青年窥探妓院。他们被一名军官发现，该军官拔出手枪前往该处。
“我们没有做任何冒犯您的事”，女房客说道。随后听到了打耳光的声音。当晚，两组日本海军陆战队员包围了该房屋，搜查了该处并恐吓屋内人员。

北四川路上有一所中国学校。对面是一户日本人家。
突然接到电话指控学生偷看一名正在洗澡的日本妇女。
调查显示，当学生们在自娱自乐时，对面的日本妇女正在洗澡。
当晚，三组日本海军陆战队员骑摩托车到达学校并搜查了学校。
次日早晨，两名学生来到学校，称一名日本浪人抢走了一个书包。

January 11, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

Hwa Tung Yen Pao dated January 10 :-

PURCHASE OF OLD COTTON, BRASS AND IRON

Of late the subjects of a certain nation have engaged a large number of Chinese traitors to purchase large quantities of used cotton, old fishing nets and old brass and iron in Shanghai, all of which are materials indispensable for the manufacture of arms and armaments. Many of the traitors who have been well paid have established shops in various parts of Shanghai and have engaged persons to visit alleyways to buy such materials. Hence the presence of so many itinerant hawkers in Chinese controlled territory and the Settlements.
It is learned that as soon as these materials have been purchased, they are placed on warships for transportation in order to evade inspection by Customs officials.

China Evening News published the following article on Jan. 10 :-

"SEARCH PARTY"

The other day the writer of this article happening to pass by the corner of North Szechuen Road and Range Road noticed a party of Japanese marines in full military kit and armed with rifles with fixed bayonets, accompanied by a number of tanks and military trucks laden with armed marines pass recklessly through the Settlement.
When he reached the corner of Dixwell Road, he suddenly found himself face to face with several armed marines who had approached from the corner of the XX Company. With their fixed bayonets, they stood in his way and shouted: "Stop, Chinese!"
He at once obeyed as did other Chinese pedestrians who happened to be near that place. They then searched him, after which they struck him in the posterior with the butts of their rifles and cursed him saying: "Chinese pig, get away!"
Just at about this time, a fruit hawker happened to approach. The marines approached and overturned one of the baskets, thereby scattering all the bananas and pears over the ground.
Noticing this, one of the on-lookers who stood near the writer of this article angrily said to himself in a low voice: "There is no justice at all. The only way is to fight them." The writer of the article did not venture a reply.

收购旧棉花、黄铜和铁器

近来，某国国民雇佣大量中国奸徒在上海收购大量废旧棉花、旧渔网以及旧黄铜和铁器，这些均为制造军火武器所不可或缺的材料。许多受重金收买的奸徒在上海各处开设店铺，并雇人深入里弄购买此类物资。因此，在华界及租界内出现了如此众多的流动小贩。

日前，本文作者偶然经过北四川路与靶子路（Range Road）转角处，注意到一队全副武装、手持装有刺刀步枪的日本海军陆战队士兵，在数辆坦克和载有武装陆战队员的军用卡车的伴随下，肆无忌惮地穿过租界。

注意到这一幕，站在本文作者附近的一名旁观者低声愤怒地自言自语：“简直没有公理。唯一的办法就是跟他们拼了。”本文作者未敢作答。

Arrest of a foreigner named Henry Hellssen,

Copenhagen, Denmark, by a Japanese Naval sentry
at the corner of North Yangtzse and Nanzing Roads

At 4.20p.m. 15/10/36, a telephone message was received
at this Station from J.P.C.14 on duty at the Japanese
Consulate, reporting to the effect that he had seen a
foreigner arrested by a Japanese Naval sentry at Nanzing
and North Yangtse Roads corner, and taken to H.I.J.M.S.
"Izumo", for taking photograph of the "Izumo".

Upon receipt of this message, J.D.C.22 and the under-
signed proceeded to the "Izumo" in order to ascertain the
matter, but on arrival at the ship it was found that the
foreigner in question had already been handed over to the
Japanese Consulate for enquiry.

The detectives then proceeded to the Consulate, where
it was found that the foreigner had already been released.
Enquiries at the Consulate ascertained that Senior
Consul Fukui interviewed the foreigner in question and
after taking his name as above, he was allowed to go.

Although the Naval authorities declined to give
details of the matter, it was ascertained that the foreigner
was attempting to take a photograph of the "Izumo" with
his Leica camera and was arrested by the sentry.

TRANSLATION: From the German daily newspaper "Ostasiatischer Lloyd"
October 3, 1936.
----------

The German photographer, Mr. Jordan, was detained yesterday
afternoon by the Japanese Marines.

Mr. Jordan was returning at 5 o'clock from a visit to a friend
in Boone Road when he observed the barricades in the streets.

As he had his camera with him, he wished to take a photograph
and while in the act of fixing up his camera some twenty Japanese
marines immediately made their appearance two of whom suddenly sprang
upon him and seized him by the wrist. Protesting violently against
this treatment Jordan struggled violently and extricated himself,
whereupon two Japanese officers demanded that he accompany them to
the nearest marine post.

As no understanding could be reached, even when Jordan showed his
visiting card, the Hongkew Police Station was communicated with, which
latter detailed several men and a British Police Officer to the scene.

Mr. Jordan explained to this latter the circumstances of the case
and complained about the treatment, pointing out at the same time,
that everybody had the right to take photographs furthermore, he
explained that photography is his profession.

The Police Officer enquired if he had taken photographs of the
Japanese Marines or barricades, to which Mr. Jordan replied in the
negative, explaining that the Marines had prevented him from doing
this. The Police officer then assured the Japanese officers that no
photographs had been taken by Mr. Jordan. However, the Japanese wanted
to take both the camera and the film.

Mr. Jordan was ultimately liberated and, at the request of the
Police officer, went to the Chinese Authorities to whom he reported
the particulars of the event.

This is not the first time the Japanese have assumed the right
to arrest journalists - especially German journalists.

We are in China, not in Japan, where the Japanese naturally can
annoy travellers as much as they please. It has to be said once for
all that the Japanese will lose the very last vestige of sympathy.

德国摄影师乔丹先生（Mr. Jordan）于昨日下午被日本海军陆战队扣留。

乔丹先生下午5时从布恩路（Boone Road）的一位朋友处返回途中，观察到街道上的路障。

由于他随身携带相机，希望拍摄照片，正当他调整相机时，约二十名日本海军陆战队员立即出现，其中两人突然扑向他并抓住他的手腕。乔丹强烈抗议这种对待，激烈挣扎并挣脱出来，随后两名日本军官要求他随他们前往最近的海军哨所。

由于即使乔丹出示名片也无法达成谅解，遂联系虹口警察局，该局派遣数名警员及一名英国警官前往现场。

乔丹向该英国警官说明了案件情况并对所受待遇提出投诉，同时指出任何人都有权拍照，此外他还解释摄影是他的职业。

警官询问他是否拍摄了日本海军陆战队或路障的照片，乔丹回答没有，并解释说海军陆战队阻止了他这样做。随后警官向日本军官保证乔丹先生未拍摄任何照片。然而，日本人仍想没收相机和胶卷。

乔丹最终获释，并应警官要求，前往中国当局处报告了事件详情。

这并非日本人首次擅自行使逮捕记者的权利——尤其是德国记者。

我们身在中国，而非日本，在日本，日本人自然可以随心所欲地骚扰旅客。必须一劳永逸地指出，日本人将失去仅存的最后一丝同情。

benutzen, um eine Aufnahme zu machen. In diesem
Augenblick rueckte eine etwa 20 Mann starke Abtei-
lung japanischer Marinesoldaten an, die er eben-
falls noch mit auf den Film bekommen wollte.
Waehrend er seinen Apparat einstellte, sprangen
ploetzlich zwei der Soldaten auf ihn zu und
packten ihn beim Handgelenk. Jordan pro-
testierte heftig gegen diese Behandlung und riss
sich los. Darauf forderte ihn ein Offizier auf,
mit in eine in der Naehe gelegene Wachstube zu
kommen. Da es nicht gelang, eine Verstaendigung
herbeizufuehren und auch das Vorzeigen der Visi-
tenkarte des Deutschen nichts nuetzte, wurde die
Hongkew-Polizeistation angerufen, die sofort einige
Leute entsandte, darunter einen englischen Offizier.
Diesem erklaerte Jordan der Vorfall, wobei
er betonte, dass es das Recht jedes Passanten sei,
auf jeder Strasse Aufnahmen zu machen, ausserdem
sei dass ein Beruf. Der Offizier fragte, ob er von
der japanischen Abteilung und den spanischen
Reitern bereits eine Aufnahme gemacht habe.
Dies konnte Jordan verneinen, da ihn die Soldaten
daran verhindert hatten. Der Englaender gab da-
raufhin den Japanern die Versicherung ab, dass
keine Aufnahme gemacht worden sei. Diese
hatten den Apparat und den Film beschlagnahmen
wollen, gaben aber nun den Verhafteten frei, der
in der chinesischen Polizeistation auf Wunsch des
Offiziers einen Bericht ueber den Vorfall zu
Protokoll gab.
*
Es ist nicht das erste Mal, dass sich die
Japaner in Shanghai das Recht herausnehmen,
Journalisten, im besonderen deutsche Jour-
nalisten zu verhaften, obwohl sie nichts
anderes taten als ihre Berufspflicht erfüllten.
Im uebrigen befinden wir uns in China und
nicht in Japan, wo es den Japanern natuerlich
frei steht, reisende Auslaender rigorosen
und kleinlichen Untersuchungen zu unter-
werfen. Es muss ein fuer allemal gesagt
werden, dass die Japaner sich bei Wieder-
holung derartiger Uebergriffe und willkuer-
licher Behandlung der Gefahr aussetzen, sich
restlos alle Sympathien zu verscherzen, die sie
unter den an sich ihnen noch wohlgesinnte-.
Auslaendern Shanghais noch besitzen.
Jedenfalls ist mit Sicherheit anzunehmen,
dass sich deutsche Pressevertreter auf chinesi-
schem Boden in Ausuebung ihrer Berufs-
pflichten keinen anderen Beschraenkungen
unterwerfen als den von den zustaendigen
Behoerden erlassenen. Zudem ist nicht einzu-
sehen, mit welchem Recht japanische Presse-
vertreter auf chinesischem Boden unbehelligt
von japanischen Soldaten, die hier keine Zu-
staendigkeit haben, ihre Berufspflichten
ungehindert erfüllen duerfen, waehrend es
deutschen und den Pressevertretern anderer
Nationalitaeten verwehrt sein soll.
(Die Schriftleitung)

一名德国人被日本人
逮捕。
德国摄影师乔丹于
昨日下午被日本士兵逮
捕。乔丹在拜访一位熟
人后，于5点钟经过布恩
路（Boone Road），在那
里他看到了西班牙式骑
兵拒马。由于他随身携
带照相机，他想利用这
个机会拍一张照片。就
在此时，一支约20人的
日本海军陆战队分队开
进，他也想把他们拍进
胶片里。当他正在调整
相机时，突然有两名士
兵扑向他并抓住了他的
手腕。乔丹对这种对待
表示强烈抗议并挣脱开
来。随后一名军官要求
他随其前往附近的一处
岗亭。由于未能达成谅
解，且出示德国人的名
片也无济于事，遂致电
虹口警察局，该局立即
派遣了几个人，其中包括
一名英国警官。
乔丹向这位警官解释了
事件经过，并强调每个
路人都有权在任何街道
上拍照，此外这也是他
的职业。警官问他是否
已经拍摄了日本分队和
西班牙式骑兵拒马。乔
丹予以否认，因为士兵
们阻止了他这样做。英
国人随即向日本人保
证，并未进行拍摄。日
本人本想没收相机和胶
卷，但此时释放了被捕
者，被捕者应警官要求
在中国警察局就事件经
过做了笔录。
*
这并非日本人在上海
第一次擅自行使逮捕记
者的权利，特别是德国
记者，尽管他们所做的
不过是履行其职业义务。
此外，我们身在中国，
而非日本，在日本，日
本人自然有权对旅行
的外国人进行严厉且
琐碎的检查。必须一劳
永逸地指出，如果日本
人再次发生此类越权行
为和任意对待，他们将
面临彻底丧失在上海外
侨中仅存的好感的危
险，尽管这些外侨原本
对他们是抱有好感的。
无论如何，可以肯定地
认为，德国新闻界代表
在中国领土上履行其职
业义务时，除了服从有
关当局颁布的限制外，
不会接受其他任何限
制。此外，看不出有何
理由允许日本新闻界代
表在中国领土上不受在
此并无管辖权的日本士
兵的干扰而自由履行其
职业义务，而德国及其
他国籍的新闻界代表却
被禁止这样做。
（编辑部）

marines on Dixwell Road and removed to Japanese Naval Landing

subsequently sent to the Shanghai Municipal Police who
released them at 7 p.m. the same day.

Another Chinese Arrested

Yesterday morning a man named Liu (刘),
while reading a notification posted up by the Bureau of
Public Safety at the Tiendong Road Bridge, was arrested
by Japanese marines and taken to their headquarters. He
was released at 4 p.m. the same day.

NIPPO

CHINESE PEACE PRESERVATION CORPS ILLEGALLY DETAINS
JAPANESE DANCING PARTNERS

At about 3 a.m. October 1 a
Japanese dancing partner named Kondo and her sister,
also a dancing partner, both of the Happy Land Dance Hall,
on North Szechuen Road, were taken at the point of drawn
pistols to the Headquarters of the Peace Preservation
Corps by members of the Corps as they were returning to
their home at No. 25 Paosan Road. The girls were
detained until 7 a.m. on the pretext of according them
protection. The girls immediately reported the incident
to the Japanese Consular Police after their release.

BRITISH SUBJECT ABUSES A MEMBER OF JAPANESE LANDING
PARTY; HONGKEW POLICE INVESTIGATES

At 9 a.m. October 2 a second
class Japanese sailor named Mori was on guard duty at
the corner of Range Road and North Szechuen Road when
a European pushed the sailor who was standing in front
of the Sze Ming Bank leaving a space of about one foot
between his back and the wall. The European passed
behind the sailor saying, "Get away" and pushed away the
sailor's rifle with his left hand. The European then
proceeded to the entrance of an alleyway at the corner
of the Chuwa Apartment House on Range Road where he bought a
newspaper. Then passing in front of the sailor on his
way back, he said to the sailor in English, "You get away
from here. This is Chinese territory". At this moment
a Filipino and a Japanese dressed in Kimono interpreted
the words of the European to the sailor. Realising that
the words were insulting to the Japanese Landing Party,
the sailor ordered the European to stop. At this juncture,
a Japanese named S. Matsumoto of Lane 142 No. 20 Sevard
Road, who happened to pass by, attempted to stop the
European but the latter struck Matsumoto in the face
with a tin can. Two other Japanese named Atachi, 40,
an employee of the Dai Ko Yoko, No. 12 Cart Lin Lue(?)
and C. Kihara, age 34, of the Kimura Yoko on Woosung Road,
seized the European under the signal tower at the crossing
of Range Road and North Szechuen Road. The European
was taken to the marine post where he was handed over to
the Hongkew Police at 10.30 a.m. The police investigation
revealed that the European in question is an ex-captain
named Thomson(?), age 60, British subject. It is
reported that on August 13, 1935(?) he used abusive language
towards a Japanese sailor in the Quinsan Garden for which
he was taken to Hongkew Station. The police are making
further inquiries.

中华和平维持团非法拘禁日本舞女

10月1日凌晨3时许，四川北路“快乐世界”舞厅的日本舞女近藤（Kondo）及其同样身为舞女的妹妹，在返回宝山路25号家中途中，被和平维持团成员持枪胁迫带至和平维持团总部。女孩们以受到保护为借口被扣留至上午7时。女孩们获释后立即向日本领事警察报告了这一事件。

英籍人士辱骂日本登陆队成员；虹口警察局展开调查

10月2日上午9时，一名名叫森（Mori）的二等日本水兵在兰路（Range Road）与四川北路拐角处执勤，当时一名欧洲人推搡站在四明银行前的这名水兵，使其背部与墙壁之间留出约一英尺的空间。该欧洲人从水兵身后走过，说道：“走开”，并用左手推开水兵的步枪。随后该欧洲人前往兰路朱华公寓（Chuwa Apartment House）拐角处的一条弄堂入口购买了一份报纸。然后在返回途中经过水兵面前时，他用英语对水兵说：“你从这里走开。这是中国的领土”。此时，一名菲律宾人和一名身穿和服的日本人将该欧洲人的话翻译给水兵听。水兵意识到这些话是对日本登陆队的侮辱，便命令该欧洲人停下。就在此时，碰巧路过的住在西华德路（Sevard Road）20号142弄的日本人松本 S.（S. Matsumoto）试图拦住该欧洲人，但后者用一只锡罐击打了松本的面部。另外两名日本人，即大古洋行（Dai Ko Yoko，地址：卡林路(?)12号）雇员、40岁的阿达奇（Atachi），以及吴淞路木村洋行（Kimura Yoko）34岁的木原 C.（C. Kihara），在兰路与四川北路交叉口的信号塔下抓住了该欧洲人。该欧洲人被带至海军哨所，并于上午10时30分移交给虹口警察局。警方调查显示，该欧洲人是一名名叫汤姆森（Thomson?）的前船长，60岁，英籍人士。据报道，他曾于1935年8月13日（？）在昆山花园对一名日本水兵使用辱骂性语言，为此曾被带至虹口警局。警方正在作进一步查询。

anti-Japanese pamphlet and were now detained in Kashing
Road Police Station. Acting on instructions from C.D.I.
Ross, D.S. Lockwood and Clerk Wong Chia-tsing attended and

At about 3.30 p.m. October 1, three male Chinese

(新生) Book Company, North Honan Road, and the Poh Sing
(北新) Book Store, Foochow Road; Tseu Kan-ling (周幹林),

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY. OCTOBER 2, 1936

Japanese Detain
Newspaper Men
Taking Pictures

Foreigner and Chinese Held
in Miller Road

FILMS ARE CONFISCATED
BY MARINES

Two employees of the "North-China Daily News," a foreign reporter and a Chinese photographer, were detained at the Japanese Landing Party temporary post at 83 Miller Road for about three-quarters of an hour yesterday afternoon, because they attempted to obtain pictures of the barbed-wire entanglement erected at the intersection of Miller and Minghong Roads, near the Hongkew Police Station. The two had made a tour of Chapei and Hongkew, getting news pictures, and stopped their car in Minghong Road at 4 o'clock.

The reporter, Mr. V. F. Meisling, got out with the photographer and instructed the latter to take a picture of the barrier, about which several members of the Landing Party were standing. No sooner had two views been snapped, however, than the marines, holding their rifles and bayonets at a menacing angle, approached the two men and attempted to snatch the camera from the Chinese. His companion objected and spoke in English to the officers who accompanied the marines. They did not understand and insisted that the Chinese, with his camera, be taken to the military post on the corner.

As the marines seized the arm of the Chinese and started to pull him towards the entrance to the post, the foreigner accompanied him, having meanwhile taken possession of the holder containing the films used in Minghong Road and elsewhere that afternoon. Inside the post, the two men were informed they would be questioned by an officer attached to the staff office of the Naval Landing Party, who had been summoned by military telephone. Mr. Meisling was permitted to use the ordinary telephone and notified the "North-China Daily News" office and, subsequently, the Municipal Police at Hongkew Station about what had transpired. He was unable to get a satisfactory answer from anyone present as to whether he was under arrest and he made no attempt to force the issue. The room was full of officers and men, all heavily armed, as well as a few Japanese civilians attached to the transport office.

The arrival of the staff officer and police from Hongkew Station resulted in a consultation, with the aid of a police interpreter, and Mr. Meisling was informed that the Naval Landing Party wished to interrogate him at their Headquarters in Kiangwan Road and that the films in the holder must be developed and examined by the Landing Party officials. He agreed and went to Kiangwan Road in a police car, accompanied by a Japanese superintendent, a Japanese detective, and a foreign detective. In another car were several officers of the Landing Party and Consular Police. The Chinese photographer was allowed to return to the "North-China Daily News" office, after he had given his name, age, and address to the Japanese officers.

At the Landing Party Barracks, Mr. Meisling was questioned briefly by Lieut.-Comdr. Tadano, staff officer, and told that the films would be examined and those not found objectionable returned to him through the police at Hongkew Station. He was allowed to leave at 5.05 p.m., having been under detention a little over an hour. He went with the police to Hongkew Station and made a statement to a foreign detective. An hour later the holder and the films were returned with the message that a third film had been found objectionable and hence had been confiscated. The two films returned were absolutely black and no prints could be made from them.

一外侨与一华人在
米勒路被拘

胶卷被海军陆战队
没收

《字林西报》的两名雇员，一名外籍记者和一名华人摄影师，昨天下午在米勒路83号日本海军陆战队临时哨所被扣留了约三刻钟，原因是他们试图拍摄虹口巡捕房附近米勒路与明宏路路口处设置的铁丝网障碍物。这两人此前巡视了闸北和虹口地区以获取新闻图片，并于四点钟将车停在明宏路上。

记者V. F. Meisling先生与摄影师一同下车，指示后者拍摄该障碍物的照片，当时有几名海军陆战队队员正站在障碍物旁。然而，就在刚拍完两张照片后，手持步枪并刺刀朝前呈威胁姿态的海军陆战队队员便逼近这两人，并试图从华人手中夺走相机。其同伴提出抗议，并用英语对陪同海军陆战队队员的军官讲话。对方听不懂，坚持要求将该华人及其相机带至街角的军事哨所。

当海军陆战队队员抓住华人的手臂并开始将其拉向哨所入口时，这名外籍人士随行陪同，同时他已取走了装有当天下午在明宏路及其他地方所用胶卷的底片盒。进入哨所后，两人被告知，将由一名经军用电话召来的海军陆战队参谋部军官对他们进行讯问。Meisling先生获准使用普通电话，通知了《字林西报》报社，随后又通知了虹口巡捕房的工部局警务处有关经过。他就自己是否被捕一事询问在场人员，但未得到满意答复，他也未试图强行解决此事。房间里挤满了全副武装的军官和士兵，以及几名隶属于运输部门的日本平民。

随着参谋军官和虹口巡捕房警察的到来，在一名警务翻译的协助下进行了协商，Meisling先生被告知，海军陆战队希望在其江湾路总部对他进行讯问，且底片盒中的胶卷必须由海军陆战队官员冲洗并检查。他表示同意，并在一名日本警司、一名日本侦探和一名外籍侦探的陪同下，乘坐警车前往江湾路。另一辆车上载有几名海军陆战队军官和领事警察。那名华人摄影师在向日本军官提供了姓名、年龄和地址后，获准返回《字林西报》报社。

在海军陆战队兵营，参谋军官Tadano少校对Meisling先生进行了简短讯问，并告知他将检查胶卷，并将未发现不妥的胶卷通过虹口巡捕房归还给他。他在被扣留一个多小时后，于下午5点05分获准离开。他随警察前往虹口巡捕房，并向一名外籍侦探作了陈述。一小时后，底片盒和胶卷被送回，附言称其中第三卷胶卷被认为不妥，因此已被没收。退回的两卷胶卷完全曝光变黑，无法洗印任何照片。

CHINA DAILY HERALD, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1938.

SMP, Japanese
Struggle Over
Custody Of Scot

Aged Foreigner Mixes
With Patrol, Held At
Barracks

A struggle between Shanghai Municipal Police and the Japanese Naval Landing Party about 9 o'clock yesterday morning for the custody of Mr. J Thomson, 60-year-old Scot threatened to throw Hongkew into an uproar as the aged foreigner was pulled out of the car in which he had been placed by Inspector W. Duncan officer in charge of the Hongkew Police Station, by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and hustled off to the fortress—barracks on Kiangwan Road.

After a short detention at the naval quarters Thomson was released about 10:30 o'clock yesterday morning.

According to an eyewitness of the incident, Thomson became engaged in a fight with three Japanese civilian members of the Naval Landing Party at the corner of Range and North Szechuen Roads and was arrested by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. A Sikh policeman on duty sent in a call to the Hongkew Police Station and Inspector Duncan rushed around to the scene in a motor car. Thomson was put into the car but the blue jackets demanded his custody for an alleged insult to the Landing Party. The inspector refused to give up the custody of Thomson, it is reported, and they reached into the car and pulled him bodily out into the street and then took him up to the Landing Headquarters in a naval truck

Thomson tells the story:
"I was walking down Range Road about 9 o'clock and I went to pass in back of a Japanese patrol in order to buy a morning paper from a coolie who was on the street. I had just given the coolie 10 cents, when I accidentally brushed against the butt of the man's rifle. He turned around and pressed the point of his bayonet against my stomach and jumped up and down, growling at me.

"I told him to take the bayonet away and tried to shove it away with my hand. A Japanese civilian came up from behind and seized me by the shoulder. Then several Japanese surrounded me and pressed their bayonets against my body."

"The municipal police came around and took me away, but the Japanese seized me right back from the police. I was held in the Landing Party Headquarters in a small room. They didn't do anything to me. But things have gotten pretty bad around here when a man can't walk down the street without his freedom being hampered."

《大陆报》，1938年10月3日，星期六。

工部局警务处与日军
争夺一名苏格兰人
的监护权

年老外侨卷入巡逻冲突，
被拘于兵营

昨天上午9点左右，上海公共租界工部局警务处与日本海军陆战队就一名60岁的苏格兰人J. Thomson先生的监护权发生争执，险些引发虹口地区的骚乱。当时，这名年老的外侨被虹口巡捕房主管警官W. Duncan巡官安置在汽车内，但日本海军陆战队队员将他从车中拽出，并强行带往江湾路的要塞——兵营。

Thomson在海军营地被短暂扣留后，于昨天上午10点30分左右获释。

据一位目击者称，Thomson在兰路（Range Road，即今溧阳路）与北四川路路口与三名属于海军陆战队的日本平民发生打斗，随后被日本海军陆战队队员逮捕。一名执勤的锡克教警察向虹口巡捕房发出呼叫，Duncan巡官随即驾车赶赴现场。Thomson被带上车，但身穿蓝制服的海军陆战队队员以涉嫌侮辱海军陆战队为由，要求由其监护。据报道，该巡官拒绝交出Thomson的监护权，于是他们伸手进车内，将他人身强行拖到街上，然后用一辆海军卡车将他带往海军陆战队总部。

Thomson讲述事发经过：
“我大约在9点钟沿着兰路行走，为了向街上的一名苦力买早报，我从一支日本巡逻队身后穿过。我刚付给苦力一角钱，不小心碰到了那人步枪的枪托。他转过身，用刺刀尖顶住我的肚子，跳上跳下，对我咆哮。

“我叫他把刺刀拿开，并试图用手推开。一名日本平民从后面走过来，抓住我的肩膀。接着几名日本人围住我，将刺刀抵在我的身上。”

“市政警察过来把我带走，但日本人又从警察手中把我抢了回去。我被关在海军陆战队总部的一间小屋里。他们没有对我做什么。但是这里的情况已经变得相当糟糕，一个人走在街上连自由都受到阻碍。”

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1936

"INCIDENT?"

The path of the newspaper reporter or photographer is seldom strewn with roses. Nor is it noticeably lined by bands which might give it the smoothness of a triumphant procession. On the contrary, the way is too often strewn with rocks, and lined by those who would quite willingly heave those rocks on the slightest provocation. This latter seems to have been the unfortunate experience of the reporter and the photographer of the "North-China Daily News" on Thursday at the hands of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. At a point within a pear-core's throw of Hongkew Police Station, and well within the boundaries of the International Settlement, the two men got out of a motor car to make a note, and take a photograph, of a barbed wire barricade erected by several Japanese marines at a corner much used by the general public and in place for all to see. The reporter, an American citizen, was detained, and the photographer, a Chinese, was made to hand over his camera after having been kept in one of the small Japanese Naval Party stations, which have been established all over the Hongkew district. Ironically enough for the American reporter, this district was known in the early days of Shanghai as the American Concession! Actually, of course, it never was an American Concession and the title was only a courtesy one. And equally, of course, there were no rocks heaved. The P.W.D. had seen to it that the road was in repair and there were no rocks about. Nevertheless, two members of the staff of this journal had to undergo an uncomfortable and perhaps at times alarming experience while carrying out their duties in a perfectly legitimate manner and without interference with anybody. Allowances can be made for excesses of zeal displayed by subordinates at moments of tension, and therefore too much need not be made of the incident, especially as newspaper reporters expect to encounter some risk and difficulty when they are "covering" a certain type of story. Where the rights of the press have not be fully established by custom, they are very much what the press can manage to make them. This, however, does not mean that the press may not expect to be treated with the courtesy and latitude allowed to other citizens, or not even reasonably anticipate more co-operation from the authorities of all nations in Shanghai in letting the public they serve know the facts of any situation. There was a conspicuous lapse in ordinary courtesies on Thursday, which it is hoped the Japanese will not allow to be repeated for the sake of the good name of their Landing Party and the friendliness which must exist to make life in an international community tolerable.

16855
《字林西报》，1936年10月3日，星期六

“事件”？

报纸记者或摄影师的道路很少铺满玫瑰。这条路上也没有明显的仪仗队为其增添凯旋游行般的平顺。相反，道路上往往布满石块，而路边站着的那些人只需稍加挑衅便乐意将这些石块砸过来。上周四，《字林西报》的记者和摄影师在日本海军陆战队手中似乎就遭遇了这种不幸的经历。在距离虹口捕房仅一箭之遥、且完全位于公共租界边界内的一个地点，这两人从汽车上下来，准备记录并拍摄由几名日本海军陆战队员在一个公众常用且众目睥睨的角落设置的铁丝网路障。这位美籍记者被拘留，而那位华籍摄影师在被关押在遍布虹口地区的日本海军小队哨所之一后，被迫交出了相机。颇具讽刺意味的是，对于这位美籍记者而言，该地区在上海早期被称为“美租界”！当然，实际上那里从未真正成为美租界，这一称呼仅是礼遇性的。同样，当然也没有人真的扔石头。工务处（P.W.D.）已确保道路修缮良好，周围并无石块。尽管如此，本报两名职员在以完全合法的方式履行职责且未干扰任何人的情况下，不得不经历了一段令人不适甚至有时令人惊恐的过程。我们可以体谅下属在紧张时刻表现出的过度热情，因此不必对此事过分渲染，尤其是因为报纸记者在“采访”某些类型的新闻时，本就预期会遇到一些风险和困难。在新闻界的权利尚未通过惯例完全确立的地方，这些权利很大程度上取决于新闻界自身能争取到何种程度。然而，这并不意味着新闻界不能期望获得与其他公民相同的礼貌和宽容，或者不能合理期待上海各国当局提供更多合作，以便让其服务的公众了解任何局势的事实真相。周四出现了明显的普通礼节缺失，希望日本方面为了其陆战队的良好声誉以及维持国际社区生活所必需的友好关系，不再让此类情况重演。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1936

2 Foreigners
Tangle With
Bluejackets

Briton, German Tempor-
arily Held At Naval
Landing Party

CAMERA AROUSES
IRE OF SAILORS

Thomson Said To Have
Bumped Into Gun
Of Sailor

Two foreigners went through the experience yesterday of being arrested and detained by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party in Hongkew.

They were Mr. W. Jordan, a German photographer, and Captain John Thomson, age 60, a retired British merchant marine skipper.

Mr. Jordan was walking near the corner of Boone and Miller Roads at 6 o'clock last night when the camera he was carrying apparently aroused the ire of the Nipponese. A party of bluejackets grabbed the instrument and brought him to the Naval Landing Party headquarters. He was later turned over and released about an hour later by the Hongkew Police, who intervened.

Mr. Thomson was picked up at 9 o'clock in the morning and taken to the Japanese Naval Landing Party barracks. He was released at the request of the Municipal Police at 10.30 o'clock.

Protest Lodged

Meantime, Mr. V. F. Miesling, a reporter on the North-China Daily News, who was arrested and detained by the Japanese near Ming-hong Road Wednesday afternoon, has lodged a protest with United States Consul-General Clarence E. Gauss.

According to an eye-witness of the incident, Captain Thomson stopped at an exchange shop at the corner of Range and Szechuen Roads to buy a morning newspaper. Japanese bluejackets have been on duty as sentries at this particular spot since the night of the Yalu Road shooting.

Fight Stopped

A fight developed and a Sikh police constable on duty near the intersection of the two streets called Hongkew Police Station. Detective Inspector W. Duncan, got into a station car and proceeded to the scene as fast as possible. Upon arriving there, he found the fight still in progress and getting hold of Thomson, pulled him into the car.

Captain Thomson came in for some pulling. The bluejackets demanded that the man be handed over to them. The inspector refused to give up custody of the man whereupon the bluejackets grabbed Thomson and pulled him from the car and then hustled him off to the barracks. The police then made immediate representations to the Japanese naval authorities and he was handed over. The police took him to the Hongkew Station where he made a written statement and was then released. Thomson said:

"I was walking down Range Road about 9 o'clock and I went to pass in back of a Japanese patrol in order to buy a morning paper from a coolie who was on the street. I had just given the coolie 10 cents when I accidentally brushed against the butt of the man's rifle. He turned around and pressed the point of the bayonet against my stomach and jumped up and down, growling at me.

Bayonets Press Near

"I told him to take the bayonet away and tried to shove it away with my hand. A Japanese civilian came up from behind and seized me by the shoulder. Then several Japanese surrounded me and pressed their bayonets against my body. "The municipal police came around and took me away, but the Japanese seized me right back from the police. I was held in the Landing Party Headquarters in a small room. They didn't do anything to me, but things have gotten pretty bad around here when a man can't walk down the street without his freedom being hampered."

Thomson, who had a few black and blue marks on his legs, evidently sustained when he was being pulled from Inspector Duncan's car, has been in trouble with the Japanese bluejackets before. On July 1, 1934, he was seated on a bench in Quinsan Park when two bluejackets came along and sat down beside him.

According to Thomson, the bluejackets took off their shoes and commenced cleaning their feet. He objected whereupon he alleges one of the sailors knocked him down and committed a nuisance over him.

《大美晚报》，1936年10月3日，星期六

两名外人与水兵发生冲突

英国人、德国人被日本海军陆战队暂时扣留

相机激起水兵怒火

据称汤姆森撞到了水兵的枪托

昨日，两名外人在虹口经历了被日本海军陆战队成员逮捕和拘留的过程。

他们是德国摄影师乔丹（W. Jordan）先生和60岁的英国退休商船船长约翰·汤姆森（John Thomson）上尉。

昨晚6时，乔丹先生在百老汇路（Boone Road）与密勒路（Miller Road）转角附近行走时，他携带的相机显然激怒了日本人。一群水兵夺走了相机，并将他带到海军陆战队总部。随后他被移交给介入此事的虹口捕房，约一小时后获释。

汤姆森上尉于上午9时被带走，送往日本海军陆战队兵营。应工部局警务处的要求，他于10时30分获释。

提出抗议

与此同时，《字林西报》记者梅斯林（V. F. Miesling）先生已于周三下午在明宏路（Ming-hong Road，音译）附近被日本人逮捕并拘留，他已向美国总领事高斯（Clarence E. Gauss）提出抗议。

据一位目击者称，汤姆森上尉在鸭绿江路（Yalu Road）枪击事件发生后的当晚，日本水兵一直在该特定地点担任哨兵。他在北四川路（Szechuen Road）与长治路（Range Road，音译，注：此处原文为Range，当时可能指长治路或附近路段，暂按音译处理，但结合上下文及历史地图，Range Rd通常对应长治路）转角的兑换店停下购买早报。

制止斗殴

现场发生了斗殴，一名在两街交汇处执勤的锡克族巡捕致电虹口捕房。警司邓肯（W. Duncan）登上警车，尽快赶赴现场。到达现场后，他发现斗殴仍在进行，于是抓住汤姆森，将他拉进车内。

汤姆森上尉遭到了一番拉扯。水兵要求将该男子移交给他们。警司拒绝交出对该男子的监护权，于是水兵抓住汤姆森，将他从车里拖出来，然后强行将他押往兵营。警方随即向日本海军当局提出即时交涉，随后该男子被移交。警方将他带到虹口捕房，他在那里做了书面陈述，随后获释。汤姆森说：

“我大约在9点钟沿着长治路（Range Road）走，为了从街上的一名苦力那里买一份早报，我从一队日本巡逻队身后绕过去。我刚给那苦力一角钱，就不小心碰到了那人的步枪枪托。他转过身，用刺刀尖顶住我的肚子，上下跳动，对我发出咆哮声。

刺刀逼近

“我叫他把刺刀拿开，并试图用手推开。一名日本平民从后面走过来，抓住我的肩膀。随后几名日本人围住我，将刺刀抵在我的身上。”

“工部局警察过来把我带走，但日本人又从警察手中把我抢了回去。我被关在陆战队总部的一间小房间里。他们没有对我做什么，但这里的情况已经变得相当糟糕，一个人走在街上连自由都受到阻碍。”

汤姆森腿部有几处瘀伤，显然是在被从邓肯警司的车上拖下来时造成的，他以前也曾与日本水兵发生过麻烦。1934年7月1日，他坐在昆山公园（Quinsan Park）的长椅上，两名水兵走过来坐在他旁边。

据汤姆森称，水兵脱下鞋子开始清理脚部。他提出反对，据称其中一名水手将他打倒，并在他身上做出猥亵行为。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, October 2, 1936

SMP, Japanese
Struggle Over
Custody Of Scot

Aged Foreigner Mixes
With Patrol, Held
At Barracks

MAN RELEASED
AFTER SESSION

Marines Wrest Victim
From Police Officer
During Row

A struggle between Shanghai Municipal Police and the Japanese Naval Landing Party about 9 o'clock this morning for the custody of Mr. J. Thomson, 60-year-old Scot, threatened to throw Hongkew into an uproar as the aged foreigner was pulled out of the car in which he had been placed by Inspector W. Duncan, officer in charge of the Hongkew Police Station, by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and hustled off to the fortress-barracks on Kiangwan Road.

After a short detention at the naval quarters, Thomson was released about 10:30 o'clock this morning.

Gets Into Fight

According to an eyewitness of the incident, Thomson became engaged in a fight with three Japanese civilians members of the Naval Landing Party at the corner of Range and North Szechuen Roads and was arrested by members of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. A Sikh policeman on duty sent in a call to the Hongkew Police Station and Inspector Duncan rushed around to the scene in a motor car. Thomson was put into the car, but the bluejackets demanded his custody for an alleged insult to the Landing Party. The inspector refused to give up the custody of Thomson it is reported, and they reached into the car and pulled him bodily out into the street and then took him up to the Landing Headquarters in a naval truck.

Thomson tells the story:

"I was walking down Range Road about 9 o'clock and I went to pass in back of a Japanese patrol in order to buy a morning paper from a coolie who was on the street. I had just given the coolie 10 cents, when I accidentally brushed against the butt of the man's rifle. He turned around and pressed the point of his bayonet against my stomach and jumped up and down, growling at me.

Menaced By Bayonets

"I told him to take the bayonet away and tried to shove it away with my hand. A Japanese civilian came up from behind and seized me by the shoulder. Then several Japanese surrounded me and pressed their bayonets against my body."

"The municipal police came around and took me away, but the Japanese seized me right back from the police. I was held in the Landing Party Headquarters in a small room. They didn't do anything to me. But things have gotten pretty bad around here when a man can't walk down the street without his freedom being hampered."

In Trouble Before

Thomson, who claims to be a retired sea captain, came into considerable prominence on July 1, 1934, when he was involved with a Japanese sailor in another incident in Quinsan Park where it was alleged the Japan-urnated on Mr. Thomson while he was sitting on a park bench.

Mr. Thomson is thought to have been brought before the British Consular Court some years ago on a charge of sailing an American vessel without a Master's license. He has a mate's license.

自称退休船长的汤姆森，在1934年7月1日因另一起发生在昆山公园的事件中与一名日本水手发生纠葛而备受瞩目，据称当时他正坐在公园长椅上，那名日本水手对他进行了猥亵。

JAPANESE MARINE INTERFERES WITH A BRITISH LADY.

At about 10 a.m. September 25, a slight dispute
took place in front of the Japanese Telegraph Office,
corner of East Seward Road and Boone Road (? Tiendong Road).
A British lady, aged about 30, who was passing by the
Japanese Telegraph Office, was suddenly stopped by a
Japanese marine. The lady protested against this
unreasonable interference, whereupon the Japanese marine,
who did not understand what she said, pointed his bayonet
at her chest. This infuriated the lady who, ignoring the
move, proceeded forward. The marine pushed her and this
almost caused her fall. A dispute then arose and the
lady cried loudly for help. Japanese marines stationed
inside the Telegraph Office came forward and the situation
suddenly became grave. Upon learning of the trouble, the
Municipal Police rushed to the scene and succeeded in
settling the dispute.

一位年约30岁的英国女士路过日本电报局时，突然被一名日本海军陆战队员拦住。该女士对这种无理干涉提出抗议，但该日本陆战队员听不懂她的话，竟用刺刀指向她的胸部。这激怒了该女士，她无视这一举动继续前行。该陆战队员推搡了她，导致她差点摔倒。随后双方发生争执，女士大声呼救。驻扎在电报局内的日本海军陆战队员上前支援，局势顿时变得严峻。工部局警务处获悉情况后迅速赶赴现场，成功平息了纠纷。

The following is the statement of John Thomson, age 49,
native of Great Britain taken by me Det. Insp. Duncan
at Hongkew on the 2/10/36 and interpreted by

My name is John Thomson, age 49, British, residing at 25 Young
Allen Court. I am at present unemployed.
At about 8.45 a.m. 2/10/36 I left my home and proceeded along
Quinsan Road to North Szechuen and along that road to near Range
Road when I crossed over to a shop on the west side of N. Szechuen
Road. At this shop I purchased a tin of quick oats. On leaving
the shop I crossed over to the east side and walked to Range Road
corner turning east on Range Road and walked a few yards on the
south pavement to where a coolie was seated selling newspapers.
Immediately in front of the coolie a Japanese marine armed with
rifle and bayonet was posted. He was facing North and was carrying
his rifle under his arm, the butt nearly touching the wall and the
bayonet reaching to about the edge of the pavement. It was
impossible to walk past the marine and keep on the pavement. I
tried to pass behind him as I wished to purchase a newspaper from
the coolie and my knee struck the butt of his rifle. He immediately
turned round and said something which I did not understand and at
the same time pointed his bayonet at me. He also called on a
Japanese civilian of stout build, dressed in a kimono who came up
and said something to me in Japanese. I told him to mind his own
business and to remember he was in China and not in Japan. By this
time a number of marines had gathered around me and the civilian
mentioned above searched my pockets and also took away my tin of
oats. I was pulled into the middle of the road and about that time
a Japanese marine officer arrived on the scene and I was then
pushed back on to the pavement.
Some time afterwards a party of police arrived in a car and

我叫约翰·汤姆森，49岁，英国人，居住在永年里（Young Allen Court）25号。目前失业。
1936年10月2日上午8时45分左右，我离开家，沿昆山路（Quinsan Road）走到北四川路，再沿该路走到靠近靶子路的地方，然后穿过马路到北四川路西侧的一家商店。在这家店里，我买了一罐速食燕麦片。离开商店后，我穿过马路到东侧，走到靶子路拐角处，在靶子路上向东转，沿南侧人行道走了几码，来到一个坐着卖报纸的苦力面前。
就在苦力正前方，站着一名手持步枪和刺刀的日本海军陆战队员。他面朝北，步枪夹在腋下，枪托几乎贴着墙壁，刺刀伸到人行道边缘附近。不可能既走在人行道上又从陆战队员身边经过。我想从苦力那里买份报纸，试图从他身后绕过去，结果我的膝盖撞到了他的枪托。他立刻转过身，说了一些我听不懂的话，同时用刺刀指着我。他还叫来一名身穿和服、体格壮实的日本平民，此人走过来用日语对我说了些什么。我告诉他少管闲事，并记住这里是中国，不是日本。此时，多名陆战队员围住了我，上述平民搜查了我的口袋，还拿走了我的燕麦片罐。我被拉到马路中间，就在这时，一名日本海军陆战队军官赶到现场，随后我被推回人行道。

The following is the statement of B. Bobby

At about 9am, 2/10/36, I was standing On North
Szechuen Road on the east side of the road a few yards south of
Range. I was accompanied by a Japanese male acquaintance whose
name is not known to me. At that time I observed Japanese
armed marines on duty at Range Road corner, one standing on
the south-east corner of the road intersection whilst two more
were standing on the north-east corner.

Whilst I was standing on the above corner, I
saw a Britisher whom I know as Mr Thompson, walking along Range
Road in an easterly direction. He appeared to me to be
intending to visit a small exchange shop situated on the south
side of Range Road near the south-east corner. Just as Mr
Thompson mounted the pavement at the south-east corner of Range
and North Szechuen Roads, I saw the Japanese marine on duty at
that corner, signal with his hand to one of the marines on duty
at the north-east corner. The Japanese marine who signalled
appeared to be very angry. The two marines then caught hold of
Mr Thompson by the wrists and attempted to lead him back onto
North Szechuen Road. Mr Thompson objected to this and struggled
with the marines, whereupon a further Japanese marine approached
and assisted his compatriots in holding Mr Thompson. Later three
Japanese civilians whom I do not know assisted the three marines.
Mr Thompson became very excited, therefore I told him to be calm
and await developments. I further told one of the Japanese
civilians to inform the Indian constable on traffic duty in the
" crows-nest " at North Szechuen and Range Roads. Also

当我站在上述路口时，我看见一位我认识的英国人汤普森先生（Mr Thompson），正沿靶子路向东行走。在我看来，他似乎打算去拜访位于靶子路南侧、靠近东南角的一家小兑换店。就在汤普森先生走上靶子路与北四川路交汇处的东南角人行道时，我看见在该角落执勤的一名日本海军陆战队员用手向在东北角执勤的另一名陆战队员发出信号。发出信号的日本海军陆战队员看起来非常愤怒。随后，这两名陆战队员抓住汤普森先生的手腕，试图将他带回北四川路。汤普森先生对此表示反对，并与陆战队员发生挣扎，此时又有一名日本海军陆战队员上前，协助其同胞控制住汤普森先生。后来，三名我不认识的日本平民也协助这三名陆战队员。汤普森先生变得非常激动，因此我告诉他保持冷静，等待事态发展。我还告诉其中一名日本平民，去通知在北四川路与靶子路路口“瞭望台”（crows-nest）值勤交通岗位的印度巡捕。此外

on the street corner was a Chinese Constable who tried to assist

在街角还有一名中国巡捕试图协助解决争端，但由于在场日本人的态度和人数众多，他未能做到。

过了一会儿，一辆警用摩托车抵达现场，一名身着制服的警司、一名侦探和一名日本警司将汤普森先生带上警车。在警用摩托车驶离之前，一辆载有海军陆战队员和一名陆战队军官的日本海军陆战队卡车驶近。该卡车的负责军官坚持要求先将汤普森先生送往日本海军陆战队总部，然后再移交给警方，于是汤普森先生由工部局警务处官员移交，并被带往日本总部。后来，我也乘坐一辆属于日本海军陆战队（J/N/L/Party）的摩托车被带到同一总部。

我能说流利的日语，在上述事件过程中，我了解到汤普森先生曾从在靶子路与北四川路东南角执勤的日本海军陆战队员身后经过，并在此过程中击打了该陆战队员的背部。随后，汤普森先生发表了一些言论，批评他认为日本当局在上海的专横行为，这些言论由当时在场的一名日本平民翻译给海军陆战队员听。

My name is Narayasu Adachi. I am employed in the "Tai Shin
Yoko", No.12 Hellen Terrace, off North Szechuen Road.
At about 9a.m. 2-10-36, whilst I was passing along North
Szechuen Road near Range Road corner, I was under the traffic
stand a foreigner quarrelling with three Japanese.
I approached them and asked them the cause of the trouble,
when they told me that the foreigner in question abused the
Japanese Naval sentry standing on the corner to the effect
that no Japanese sentry needed within Chinese territory so
should evacuate as soon as possible.
Ascertaining the above, I, together with the three Japanese
took the foreigner to the nearby footpath. At this juncture,
the foreigner attempted to strike me but managed to avoid his
attack. One of the Japanese, however, received a blow from
the foreigner on the forehead.
Meanwhile, an officer with two or three men of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party arrived at the scene and the foreigner was
subsequently taken away by the Naval Officer.
Above is my true statement.

我叫安彦直康（Narayasu Adachi）。受雇于北四川路旁海伦路（Hellen Terrace）12号的“泰新洋行”（Tai Shin Yoko）。
1936年10月2日上午9时许，当我经过北四川路靠近靶子路路口时，我在交通岗亭下看到一名外国人与三名日本人争吵。
我走近他们，询问争执原因，他们告诉我，该外国人辱骂站在角落的日本海军哨兵，称在中国领土内不需要日本哨兵，因此应尽快撤离。
在得知上述情况后，我与那三名日本人一起将该外国人带到附近的人行道上。就在此时，该外国人试图袭击我，但我成功避开了他的攻击。然而，其中一名日本人的额头被该外国人打了一拳。
与此同时，一名军官带着两三名日本海军陆战队士兵到达现场，该外国人随后被海军军官带走。
以上是我的真实陈述。

签名。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Masamitsu Motoyama(元山政光)
native of Japan taken by me J.D.C.22 Nakayama
at Hongkew Station on the 2-10-36 and interpreted by

My name is Masamitsu Motoyama, Japanese and I am
residing at No.237 Haining Road.
At about 9 a.m. 2-10-36, at the corner of North Szechuen
Road and Range Road, I heard one foreigner speaking to a
Japanese sailor of the Landing Party on duty there to the
effect that, the place being Chinese territory, the sailor
should withdraw from the scene to the Headquarters of the
Japanese Landing Party.
I thereupon told the sailor what the foreigner had said.
As the foreigner, sensing the matter turning worse, was
about to leave the scene across the tramway, I caught him near
the traffic stand with other three Japanese and took him to
the footpath.
In the course of this trouble, I saw the foreigner assault
one of the Japanese with a tin which he had been carrying.
He, moreover, attempted to strike all of us, but other Japanese
nearby interrupted him from doing so.
This statement is true and correct.

Signed.

以下系由元山政光（Masamitsu Motoyama）所作之供词，日本籍人士，由我 J.D.C.22 Nakayama 于1936年10月2日在虹口巡捕房录取，并由……翻译。

我叫元山政光（Masamitsu Motoyama），日本人，居住在海宁路237号。
1936年10月2日上午9时许，在北四川路与靶子路路口，我听见一名外国人对在那里执勤的日本海军陆战队水兵说话，大意是此地为中国领土，该水兵应从现场撤回到日本海军陆战队总部。
于是我告诉水兵该外国人说了什么。
由于该外国人察觉到事态恶化，正打算穿过电车轨道离开现场，我便与其他三名日本人在交通岗亭附近抓住他，并将他带到人行道上。
在这场争端中，我看见该外国人用他携带的一个铁罐袭击了一名日本人。
此外，他还试图袭击我们所有人，但附近的其它日本人阻止了他这样做。
此陈述真实无误。
